summary:
Amazonas stands under Brazil's national framework, and adds its own layer of protection. State Ordinary Law No. 3079 of 12 September 2006 prohibits discrimination on grounds of gender identity across employment, housing and other areas, and a provision in force since 2 August 2006 prohibits the manufacture, sale and distribution of symbols inciting discrimination, prejudice, hatred or violence on gender-identity grounds.

Non-binary recognition is not available in practice through Amazonas registries. In 2022 Alex Souza de Sa became the first non-binary person in the state to obtain recognition, doing so only after a rectification in Rio de Janeiro and an intervention by the Amazonas Public Defenders Office in Manaus, where no gender-neutral marker existed. Non-binary recognition in the state remains decided case by case.

Facilities are a live exposure in the state capital. On 18 October 2022 the mayor of Manaus signed a municipal law prohibiting unisex or multigender restrooms, and Equaldex records that bathroom access in Amazonas carries no explicit legal protection.

Access to gender-affirming care is contested on two fronts. On 10 June 2025 the governor of Amazonas signed Law 7552 banning gender-affirming care for minors under 18. In the opposite direction, in November 2023 the State Public Defenders Office opened a collective procedure to monitor public health services for trans and travesti people, covering hormone treatment, outpatient services and the refusal of authorisation for transsexualising surgeries including sexual reassignment surgery; after an October 2023 meeting, Manaus municipal health officials committed to dispensing standardised medications on Ambulatório Codajás prescriptions for hormone therapy and to designating reference primary-care units in each zone of the city, and the state health secretariat was required to report on gaps in equitable care and hormone therapy. In August 2024 the Federal Public Prosecutors Office recommended that Amazonas formally enable outpatient and hospital transsexualisation services, including sexual reassignment surgeries, with deadlines for approval and for presentation to the Ministry of Health.

Recorded violence against LGBTQ people in Amazonas is thin and structurally undercounted. Research published in the Brazilian Journal of Public Security finds that cases of violence against LGBTQ people in the state are underreported, and the Brazilian Public Security Forum has registered 43 cases. For 2021-2022, crimes reported in Manaus and the interior involving homosexual, lesbian, bisexual and transsexual persons accounted for 0.36% of all reports, with homophobia and transphobia motives and the categories of gender, sexuality, race and intersectionality absent from the records; LGBT victim data were few and poorly structured, victims were not infrequently recorded as perpetrators because of failures in police occurrence reports, and public agents were unprepared to handle these demands. On 5 July 2025 Fernando Vilaca de Souza was beaten and killed in Manaus after reacting to homophobic insults, with residents reporting that he had been bullied by other young people in the region.

State and municipal law also restricts LGBTQ expression and public presence. Amazonas Ordinary Law No. 6463, enacted 10 October 2023, expressly prohibits the use of neutral language, non-binary dialect or any expression departing from standard Portuguese in curricula and teaching materials of public and private educational institutions and in official documents of educational institutions and public agencies across the state. State Law 6469 of 2023 prohibits the participation of children and adolescents in pride parades, with fines of up to 10,000 reais for non-compliance. On 17 October 2024 the Legislative Assembly enacted a law prohibiting reproduction of digital media using children linked to homosexuality; it was amended on 13 December 2025 to remove the term homosexuality and instead prohibit reproduction of sexual content linked to children in cultural and artistic media.

Protection machinery exists at state level alongside those restrictions. In 2021 the State Public Defenders Office created the Sexual Diversity, Gender Identity and Citizenship Working Group, focused on human rights violations and on training security agents. In August 2024 the Amazonas State Court of Justice released the booklet Home is a Right, aimed at LGBTQ youth expelled from their homes, which states that conversion therapies are prohibited and ineffective and points readers to the Specialized Human Rights Public Defender's Office. In November 2012 a judge of the Amazonas Court of Justice authorised the state's first adoption by a same-sex couple.
tangentialFactors:
OutRight International reports that Brazil's legal advances for sexual and gender minorities face repeal pressure in a conservative Congress, so protections relied on in Amazonas are not politically settled at either level.

A Brazilian law-firm guide for expatriates notes that enforcement is uneven in practice: major cities present established legal infrastructure and broader social acceptance, while smaller cities and rural areas may carry more social friction despite identical legal rights. For Amazonas that distinction falls between Manaus, where the Public Defenders Office, the State Court of Justice and the municipal health commitments operate, and the interior, where the state's own crime records show the same provisions applied without motive categories.

The state's violence figures are raw counts without a denominator and without a trans-specific breakdown, so they cannot support a comparison with other states or a statement about relative risk to trans residents.

Residents of Amazonas are covered by Ordinary Law No. 3079 of 12 September 2006 in employment, housing and other areas on gender-identity grounds, and by the 2 August 2006 prohibition on producing or distributing symbols that incite discrimination, prejudice, hatred or violence on those grounds.

The State Public Defenders Office runs the Sexual Diversity, Gender Identity and Citizenship Working Group, created in 2021 to address human rights violations and to train security agents, and its health unit Nudesa holds the collective procedure opened in November 2023 on hormone therapy, outpatient services and refused surgical authorisations. Manaus primary-care coverage includes designated reference units per city zone and standardised hormone prescriptions under the Ambulatório Codajás arrangement agreed in October 2023.

Residents face state-level restrictions on expression and public life: Ordinary Law No. 6463 of 10 October 2023 bars neutral language and non-binary dialect from curricula, teaching materials and official documents of schools and public agencies; Law 6469 of 2023 bars children and adolescents from pride parades with fines up to 10,000 reais; and the Legislative Assembly's 17 October 2024 media law, as amended on 13 December 2025, bars reproduction of sexual content linked to children in cultural and artistic media.

LGBTQ youth expelled from home can use the Amazonas State Court of Justice booklet Home is a Right of August 2024, which states that conversion therapies are prohibited and ineffective and directs them to the Specialized Human Rights Public Defender's Office.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the age thresholds for gender-affirming care cited for Amazonas from 2 October 2025 (puberty blockers and hormones prohibited under 18, surgery from 21) derive from state Law 7552 alone or from national professional-council rules applied in the state is unresolved in the sources; Law 7552 itself is dated 10 June 2025 and covers under-18s.

The 43 registered cases of violence against LGBTQ people in Amazonas are recorded as LGBTQ-general, with no stated disaggregation for transgender victims, and the 0.36% share of total reports for 2021-2022 carries no population denominator. No source states a finding on societal tolerance of transgender people in Amazonas specifically.

The figure of a 59% rise in registry gender changes by 2024 appears in a source discussing Amazonas but its geographic scope is not stated, so it is not attributed here to the state.

Whether Manaus's 2022 unisex-restroom prohibition has been enforced against any establishment, and whether any challenge to it is pending, is not sourced.
